material: 43 mm fiber-reinforced polymer case, Corning Gorilla Glass 3 lens, 41 g with silicone band
features: Cheapest Garmin Forerunner with a barometric altimeter and gyroscope

Training Readiness, HRV Status and Garmin Coach with no subscription

Garmin Pay on both the base and Music variants

specs.batteryAlwaysOn: 4 days with always-on display — the headline 10-day figure assumes the screen is off between glances
specs.batteryGpsMultibandHours: No multiband mode exists on this watch; all-systems (L1 only) runs 14 h
specs.gnssBands: Single-band L1 multi-GNSS (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, QZSS). No L5/dual-frequency — DC Rainmaker's hands-on and the garminrumors spec wiki both confirm this; the5krunner's spec page loosely calls it 'multi-frequency', which is wrong. Multiband starts at the Forerunner 570.
specs.maps: None. Breadcrumb course-following only — no TopoActive maps, no turn-by-turn, no ClimbPro.
specs.musicStorage: Only on the $349.99 Forerunner 170 Music: 4 GB with offline Spotify, Amazon Music and Deezer. The $299.99 base model reviewed here has no music storage and no Wi-Fi.
specs.trainingPlatform: Garmin Connect is free and every core training metric — Training Readiness, Training Load, Training Status, HRV Status, Body Battery, recovery time — is Firstbeat-derived and free on the watch (Garmin bought Firstbeat in 2020). Connect+ is $6.99/mo or $69.99/yr and adds only AI wellness prompts, 3D maps, Trails+ routing, extra badges and nutrition logging — nothing a training plan depends on.
specs.externalSensors: Pairs with both ANT+ and Bluetooth chest straps, footpods and Stryd — the cheap fix for wrist-HR interval errors
specs.dataExport: Full .FIT file access over USB/MTP plus free automatic sync to Strava, TrainingPeaks, Runalyze, intervals.icu and others through Garmin Connect.

pros: Adds a barometer, gyroscope, wrist running power, Training Readiness and open-water swimming over the Forerunner 165 it replaces
Every training and recovery metric is free — Connect+ at $6.99/mo adds nothing a runner's plan depends on
Pairs with ANT+ and Bluetooth chest straps, so $60 of strap fixes the wrist sensor for intervals
20 h of GPS-only battery covers a road marathon several times over
cons: Single-band L1 GNSS only — in city streets or under canopy the trace drifts, and multiband costs $250 more (Forerunner 570)
No multisport/triathlon mode at all, so it cannot record a triathlon; DC Rainmaker flags this as the headline omission
No maps of any kind, and no turn-by-turn — breadcrumbs only
Music is a $50 upcharge: the base model has zero song storage and no Wi-Fi
The 10-day smartwatch claim drops to 4 days the moment you enable the always-on display
shortTagline: Garmin's best cheap road-running AMOLED — but single-band GPS and no triathlon mode.

specs.displayType: 1.2-in 390x390 AMOLED touchscreen with digital crown, optional always-on

specs.musicStorage: 4 GB for sideloaded MP3s played to Bluetooth headphones. No Spotify and no other streaming service.

specs.dataExport: Free .FIT and GPX export from the COROS app, plus automatic sync to Strava, TrainingPeaks, Nike Run Club, Apple Health and Health Connect.

pros: Dual-frequency L1+L5 GNSS at $249 — the single biggest accuracy upgrade you can buy at this price
31 h in the most accurate GPS mode still beats what most $500 AMOLED watches manage
32 g on the nylon band; you forget it is there on a long run
No subscription anywhere in the COROS ecosystem, and .FIT files sync free to Strava and TrainingPeaks
DC Rainmaker found the optical HR 'spot-on' through intervals — unusual for a $249 watch

No ANT+, so ANT+-only power meters and older chest straps will not pair

pros: Proper multi-band L1+L5 GNSS with SatIQ — a step change over the Forerunner 170's single-band trace

specs.displayType: 1.4-in 454x454 AMOLED touchscreen with sapphire lens, optional always-on

specs.maps: Full TopoActive topographic maps preloaded, free, with on-device routing and turn-by-turn, plus 2,000+ ski resorts and 43,000 golf courses in 32 GB

Older Elevate Gen 4 optical HR sensor, not the Gen 5 in cheaper Garmins

pros: Free global offline topo maps with street and trail names at $429 — Garmin charges $749.99 before you get maps
Titanium bezel and sapphire glass at a price where rivals use aluminium and Gorilla Glass

material: Titanium-alloy bezel with sapphire crystal lens; approximately 49 g without strap (48 mm)
features: 3,000-nit 1.5-in AMOLED behind sapphire crystal
Free offline contour maps with turn-by-turn, POI search and auto-rerouting
10 ATM plus EN13319 freediving certification to 45 m
Dual-band GNSS with 38 h of precision GPS
Zepp OS apps for TrainingPeaks, Stryd and Wild.AI

specs.displayType: 1.5-in AMOLED, up to 3,000 nits, sapphire crystal lens, optional always-on
specs.batteryAlwaysOn: Amazfit's 25-day figure is typical use; heavy use is rated 10 days and one reviewer measured about 18 days alongside 14 h of accurate GPS. Amazfit does not publish a separate always-on display figure.
specs.gnssBands: Dual-band (L1+L5) circularly-polarised GNSS. The 85 h headline is the power-saving GPS mode; the accurate dual-band mode is 37-38 h on the 48 mm and about 29 h on the 44 mm.
specs.maps: Free offline contour maps with turn-by-turn, POI search, round-trip routing and auto-rerouting — but you must select and download each map region inside the Zepp phone app and transfer it across. Android Police called the process 'messy and time-consuming' with vague instructions.
specs.musicStorage: Onboard storage for sideloaded MP3 files played to Bluetooth headphones. No Spotify and no streaming services.
specs.trainingPlatform: The Zepp app and core training/recovery metrics are free. Zepp Aura, the AI sleep and coaching layer, is a paid subscription; the training data itself is not gated behind it.
specs.externalSensors: Bluetooth only — no ANT+. BLE chest straps and Stryd pods pair through Zepp OS.
specs.dataExport: Free sync to Strava, adidas Running, Apple Health and Google Health Connect, plus a TrainingPeaks Zepp OS app; .FIT export via the Zepp app

pros: 38 h of dual-band GPS and 25 days of typical use for $399.99 — Garmin charges $1,199.99 for 30 h of multiband
A 3,000-nit AMOLED behind sapphire with a titanium-alloy bezel at half the price of rivals with those materials
Free offline contour maps with genuine auto-rerouting, which even the $749.99 Forerunner 970 does not beat on price
10 ATM plus EN13319 freediving certification to 45 m, unusual at any price
cons: Maps must be picked and downloaded region-by-region in the Zepp phone app then transferred — reviewers describe the process as messy and poorly documented
The 85 h battery headline is the power-saving GPS mode; the dual-band mode you would actually race on is 38 h
No ANT+ and no Spotify or any streaming service — sideloaded MP3 only
Zepp's software ecosystem and analytics are a clear step behind Garmin and COROS, and the app is cluttered
48 mm and chunky; reviewers found it too bulky for 24-hour wear
shortTagline: Flagship materials, maps and 38 h of dual-band GPS for $399 — with clumsy map downloads.
